# A check that excludes one generated filename goes stale the moment the generator writes a second

**Observed:** `tests/test_jit_layer_set_sync_702.py` compared the `01-oss` layer on disk against the
set `scripts/oss_rules.py` ships, excluding exactly one filename — `00-index.tsv`, spelled as the
constant `INDEX`. A newer `claude-jit-context` rebuild writes a **second** generated index,
`01-paths.tsv`, into the same directories. The check reported it as
`in this repository's layer and shipped by nobody`.

**What it cost:** one CI round, four red legs, on a pull request whose subject was unrelated. The
finding was well-written and pointed at a real invariant; it just described a generated artifact
rather than a rule.

**How it was confirmed:** deleting the file made the check pass, and `rebuild-tsv.sh` recreated it
immediately, so the failure was reproducible on demand and would have hit the next contributor who
rebuilt the index.

**The shape:** an exclusion list written as a name is a bet that the tool on the other side never
adds a second file. A rule in a jit layer is always a `.md`, so the class — "not a `.tsv`" — is the
boundary that cannot go stale this way. Excluding by name is the same defect as filtering a survey
by suffix: it is not wrong about the file it names, it is silent about the file it does not.

**Unjudged:** the general form ("exclude the class the invariant is about, not the instance you have
seen") may already be covered by the `shell-sources-survey.md` rule, which is about the same mistake
one dimension over. Possibly a merge rather than a new rule.
